findings.reason: Untrusted source: bnad_debugfs_write_regrd is the .write handler of the debugfs 'regrd' node (registered via bnad_debugfs_op_regrd with .write = bnad_debugfs_write_regrd at line 454, file created by debugfs_create_file at line 521), so an unprivileged-enough writer with debugfs access controls both nbytes and every byte written. Violated invariant: memdup_user(buf, nbytes) at line 315 allocates exactly nbytes bytes with no NUL terminator and no in-bounds-NUL check, yet sscanf(kern_buf, "%x:%x", ...) at line 319 is a C-string consumer that scans until NUL; the allocated size is validated-equals-used only for the copy length, not for termination. Unsafe use: sscanf walks past the end of the nbytes-sized kmalloc allocation whenever the user data contains no NUL byte, an out-of-bounds heap read (KASAN slab-OOB; info leak/crash), exactly mirroring the seed's scsi bfa bfad_debugfs_write_regrd (seed fix memdup_user -> memdup_user_nul). Counterevidence checked: file contains zero memdup_user_nul/strndup_user calls (grep count 0), no count+1 allocation, and no memchr/NUL validation between copy and sscanf; the identical pattern repeats at lines 375/379 in bnad_debugfs_write_regwr. Impact requires write access to the driver's debugfs node, but the code path and missing terminator are unambiguous.

Same mechanism in bnad_debugfs_write_regwr (.write of the debugfs 'regwr' node, bnad_debugfs_op_regwr at line 462, mode 0200): memdup_user(buf, nbytes) at line 375 allocates exactly the attacker-supplied nbytes with no terminator slot, then sscanf(kern_buf, "%x:%x", &addr, &val) at line 379 consumes it as a NUL-terminated C string and reads past the allocation when no NUL exists in the user bytes. No memdup_user_nul, strndup_user, len+1 allocation, or NUL check exists in the file; the second sscanf read is bounded by the return-code check rc<2 only after the OOB scan already happened.

Untrusted source: crw_inject_write is the .write handler of the s390 CIO debugfs 'crw_inject' node (crw_fops .write = crw_inject_write at line 152, debugfs_create_file("crw_inject", 0200, ...) at line 161), gated only by the cio_inject_enabled static key which the same debugfs directory can enable. Violated invariant: vmemdup_user(buf, lbuf) at line 98 duplicates exactly lbuf attacker bytes with no NUL terminator, then sscanf(buffer, ...) at line 102 scans for seven %x conversions, reading until NUL past the allocation end. Unsafe use and impact are identical in kind to the seed (OOB heap read, KASAN slab-OOB); no vmemdup_user_nul equivalent, memdup_user_nul, or NUL check exists in the function, and kvfree happens only after the parse. Lower practical exposure than the bna finding (s390-only, debugfs-gated) but the code-level invariant violation is unambiguous.

Untrusted source: ice_debugfs_module_write is the .write handler of ice fwlog module debugfs nodes (ice_debugfs_module_fops at line 202). Violated invariant: after rejecting count>8, it does cmd_buf = memdup_user(buf, count) at line 174 (exactly count bytes, no terminator) and then sscanf(cmd_buf, "%s", user_val) at line 184, a string-scan that runs until NUL and can read past the count-byte allocation; the %s also risks overflowing the 16-byte user_val stack buffer when count is 8 non-space bytes, though user_val is declared char user_val[16] so count<=8 bounds that. Medium confidence: the memdup_user/sscanf-on-unterminated-buffer mechanism is literal, but count is capped at 8 which limits the OOB read to a few bytes past a small kmalloc allocation, and slab rounding may mask it; three sibling handlers (lines 260/264, 335/339, 431/435 with caps 4 and similar) repeat the pattern. No NUL-termination or memchr check appears between copy and parse in any of them.

Untrusted source: reached from the QAT char-device ioctl path adf_ctl_ioctl (IOCTL_CONFIG_SYS_RESOURCE_PARAMETERS -> adf_ctl_ioctl_dev_config -> adf_copy_key_value_data), so the caller fully controls the adf_user_cfg_key_val and adf_user_cfg_section structs copied with copy_from_user. Violated invariant: the copied structs embed char key[64] and char val[64] (adf_cfg_user.h; ADF_CFG_MAX_STR_LEN 64) with no guarantee of in-bounds NUL, and the section name is likewise char name[64]. Unsafe use: adf_add_key_value_data passes these arrays as const char* to adf_cfg_add_key_value_param, which calls strscpy(key_val->key, key, sizeof) (line 268) and later strcmp-based lookups via adf_cfg_key_value_find/strcmp(ptr->key, key) (adf_cfg.c ~line 193) and adf_cfg_sec_find/strcmp(ptr->name, sec_name) (~line 206) on the unterminated user arrays, reading past the 64-byte fields and past the 56-112 byte copy_from_user stack/heap objects; strscpy itself scans the source until NUL or dest-limit, and strcmp/strscpy-with-larger-src walk the source OOB. Counterevidence checked: sizeof(key_val) is copied whole (fixed-size, not length-attacked), but nothing validates key/val/name termination before the string helpers run, so the invariant violation is real; medium confidence because the OOB read is bounded by strscpy's destination limit in the strscpy path and only the strcmp paths scan unbounded, and QAT ioctl access requires the qat device node.

candidates.reason: bnad_debugfs_write_regrd: memdup_user(buf, nbytes) line 315 into exactly-nbytes allocation, sscanf(kern_buf, ...) line 319 with no terminator; reported as finding.
bnad_debugfs_write_regwr: memdup_user(buf, nbytes) line 375 then sscanf(kern_buf, ...) line 379, same missing-NUL invariant; reported as finding.
crw_inject_write debugfs .write: vmemdup_user(buf, lbuf) line 98 then seven-conversion sscanf at line 102 on unterminated buffer; reported as finding.
ice_debugfs_module_write (and siblings at 264, 339, 435): memdup_user(buf, count) then sscanf(cmd_buf, "%s", ...) with no terminator; count capped small so bounded OOB; reported at medium confidence.
ioctl-copied adf_user_cfg_key_val/section char arrays (key/val/name, 64 bytes each, no termination guarantee) flow into strscpy and strcmp helpers in adf_cfg.c; reported at medium confidence.

rvu_dbg_qsize_write uses memdup_user(buffer, count + 1) at line 1001 and explicitly sets cmd_buf[count] = '\0' at line 1004 before strchr/strsep, so termination is guaranteed; the +1 slot is exactly the seed's fix primitive.

btrfs_ioctl_resize and all other vol_args users call btrfs_check_ioctl_vol_args_path (line 230) which requires memchr(vol_args->name, 0, sizeof(...)) != NULL before any strcmp/strchr/kstrtoull, enforcing in-bounds NUL; struct embeds name[BTRFS_PATH_NAME_MAX+1] anyway.

hidp_setup_hid memdup_user(req->rd_data, req->rd_size) feeds hid_parse_report which is a binary HID descriptor parser with explicit length, not a NUL-terminated string consumer; req->name copied with strscpy from a fixed ioctl struct path.

snd_timer_user_ginfo memdup_user(_ginfo, sizeof(*ginfo)) copies a fixed-size struct whose id/name are kernel-fixed arrays; strscpy destination is the same struct copied back, source t->id is kernel-maintained terminated data.

ip_vs_genl_new_daemon strscpy from nla_data(IPVS_DAEMON_ATTR_MCAST_IFN) is protected by nla_policy NLA_NUL_STRING with len limit (ip_vs_daemon_policy line 3199), so netlink guarantees NUL termination before use.

strcmp(name, nla_data(link[TIPC_NLA_LINK_NAME])) is preceded by string_is_terminated(name, len) check on the request side; the nla_data side comes from kernel-generated TIPC_NLA_LINK_NAME attributes via nla_put_string.

rproc_cdev_write copy_from_user(cmd, buf, len) with len <= sizeof(cmd) uses strncmp(cmd, "start", len) bounded by len, not strlen on the user data; the ioctl handler copies a fixed s32 and does no string ops.

tool_peer_mw_trans_write copies min(size, sizeof(buf)-1) into buf and sets buf[buf_size]='\0' before sscanf, guaranteeing termination; the other copy_from_user (line 782) is a pure memcpy_toio data path with no string use.
pstore_write_user_compat vmemdup_user result is passed to record->psi->write as a raw byte buffer with record->size length; no C-string parser consumes it (no sscanf/strlen/strcmp on the buffer).
sscanf target is the compile-time constant HPSA_DRIVER_VERSION string, not user data.
slcan_ioctl SIOCGIFNAME strlen is on kernel-maintained sl->dev->name, not on user-copied data.

limitations: Searched only snapshot s03 per intent; other snapshots are out of scope for i013.

The ioctl/sockopt/netlink portion of the branch was searched by pattern (ioctl function bodies containing copy_from_user/memdup_user plus string ops, setsockopt files, and direct nla_data->string-helper sites) rather than reading every ioctl handler in the tree; a variant hidden inside a deeply inlined helper called from an ioctl without copy_from_user in the same function body could be missed.

io_uring, compat ioctl wrappers delegating to common handlers, and drivers that parse strings inside vendor library code called from ioctls (other than the QAT path examined) were not exhaustively audited.

The ice and QAT findings are medium confidence: ice bounds count to <=8 so the OOB read is only a few bytes past a small kmalloc object (slab rounding may mask it), and QAT's strcmp/strscpy overflows depend on the 64-byte key/val/name arrays lacking NUL, which was verified structurally but not by dynamic test.

Impact of the two high-confidence bna/s390 findings and the ice/QAT findings requires access to the respective debugfs nodes (bna, ice, cio_inject, typically root-only) or the QAT device node; the code-level missing-terminator invariant is nonetheless identical to the seeded CVE mechanism.
